content.user_title: Shape Ideas Into Clear Technical Designs
content.value_statement: Early feature ideas often lack clear requirements, trade-offs, and validation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through structured questions, alternatives, and design checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Guides a three-phase process for understanding, exploration, and design presentation.
Prompts one clarifying question at a time with structured choice examples.
Compares two or three architecture options with pros, cons, and complexity.
Presents design sections with validation checkpoints before implementation planning.
Provides reusable design document and decision matrix templates.
Includes example sessions for authentication storage and real-time dashboard decisions.
limitations: It does not implement code or run technical validation by itself.
Its output depends on accurate user answers about goals and constraints.
The examples focus on product and engineering design workflows.
Security guidance is planning support, not a formal security review.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Feature Concept
use_cases.description: Turn a rough product idea into goals, constraints, success criteria, and open questions before sprint planning.

use_cases.title: Compare Architecture Options
use_cases.description: Evaluate competing technical approaches with clear trade-offs, complexity estimates, and validation checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Solo Build Plans
use_cases.description: Convert a vague app idea into an actionable design summary before writing implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Rough Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help me clarify this idea: [idea]. Ask one question at a time before proposing solutions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Approaches
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for choosing a direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to compare two or three approaches for [feature]. Include trade-offs, complexity, and a recommended path.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Design Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for documenting a selected approach.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to turn [chosen approach] into a concise design document. Validate each section before moving forward.

prompt_templates.title: Stress-Test an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to challenge this proposed design: [design]. Find assumptions, missing constraints, alternatives, and implementation risks.

output_examples.input: I want to add authentication, but I do not know where to store session data.
output: A focused question about storage requirements and security needs.
A comparison of cookie sessions, local tokens, and server-side sessions.
A validated design summary covering logout behavior, notifications, and cookie protections.

output_examples.input: We need a real-time dashboard and are unsure between polling, SSE, or WebSockets.
output: A trade-off table comparing latency, infrastructure complexity, and scaling behavior.
A recommended approach matched to update frequency and operational constraints.
A design outline with data flow, failure handling, and rollout notes.

output_examples.input: I have a product idea but only a few rough requirements.
output: A sequence of clarifying questions about users, goals, constraints, and success criteria.
A short list of viable approaches with benefits and drawbacks.
A staged design presentation that asks for validation before implementation planning.

best_practices: Start with goals, constraints, and users before discussing architecture choices.
Keep each question scoped to one decision so answers stay actionable.
Capture accepted trade-offs in the final design summary.
anti_patterns: Skipping clarification and generating an implementation plan immediately.
Presenting only one architecture when meaningful alternatives exist.
Treating sample templates as final requirements without adapting them.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It prepares design decisions and documentation before implementation begins.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with product ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. It clarifies users, goals, constraints, success criteria, and open questions.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses markdown guidance, examples, and templates.

faq.question: How should I use the templates?
faq.answer: Use them after brainstorming to document decisions, alternatives, risks, and implementation notes.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It can surface security considerations, but expert review is still needed for high-risk systems.
